newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Controversial Russian banker denies wrongdoing.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Russian banker denies wrongdoing.

text.p: Former first deputy finance minister Andrei Vavilov, whose name has been linked to a potentially huge financial scandal in Russia, denied on Tuesday any misdoings.
"All accusations against me are groundless," Vavilov told a brief news conference in Moscow. "All laws and rules have been followed."
On Monday, Central Bank of Russia chairman Sergei Dubinin accused commercial bank Unikombank of misappropriating half a billion dollars in government money.
Dubinin said his accusations concerned the diversion of two large government payments in 1996 and 1997 intended for Moscow regional council and MAPO-MiG, manufacturer of MiG fighter aircraft.

During a supervisory check of Unikombank, the central bank said it found that it was one in a chain of banks through which the Finance Ministry forwarded state funds in the form of government MinFin bonds to Moscow region and MAPO-MiG.
When Unikombank received the bonds, it sold them and kept the proceeds, Dubinin said.
Dubinin said Vavilov, removed from the ministry in a reshuffle four months ago, had approved the payments, adding that his superior, the finance minister, had not been informed.

"When issuing budget funds, numerous breaches of accepted procedures and rules were committed at the Finance Ministry," Dubinin said in a statement. He did not say that Vavilov was to blame for the violations.
Vavilov, saying he was sure an investigation would clear his name of all accusations, said on Tuesday all top officials, including the finance minister, had known about the MAPO-MiG deal.

Vavilov also said that at his time at the ministry he considered that a number of banks had been earning "too high profits" on operations with cash surrogates and he had passed a formal request to the prosecutors to look into such cases.
